Freon-12, a type of chlorofluorocarbon (CFC), is being phased out due to its contribution to ozone layer depletion. The Montreal Protocol, an international treaty signed in 1987, aims to reduce CFC production by 50% by the end of the century. Alternative refrigerants like R-134a are being developed and used in new air-conditioning systems. However, converting older systems to use R-134a can be expensive, with costs ranging from $200 to $800. The phase-out of Freon-12 is part of a broader effort to protect the ozone layer and prevent environmental damage.
